title: Variable macros ({{setvar}}/{{getvar}}/{{addvar}}/{{incvar}}/{{decvar}}) entirely missing — contradicts the skill's persistence advice
reality: packages/shared/src/utils/macro-engine.ts implements a Variables macro category: {{setvar::name::value}} stores a value and leaves nothing in the text, {{getvar::name}} reads it, plus addvar/incvar/decvar (parser at lines 1326-1336, catalog entries at 414-415, documented in docs/prompts/macros.md). No reference file mentions any of them.
fix: Add a 'Variable macros' subsection to references/character-cards.md and cite it from decision-guide.md Q8. HIGH severity: SKILL.md's decision hierarchy item 8 tells users that persistent structured state requires 'a webhook tool + your own backend' because 'the engine's persistence is scoped to chats/characters/lorebooks'. Dynamic variables are a real in-engine state mechanism, so that advice currently over-recommends standing up a backend for state a macro could hold.

title: {{agent::TYPE}} macro missing — the injection path for agent output
reality: {{agent::TYPE}} inserts the saved/cached output of an agent or tracker type into a prompt; it renders only once the matching agent has run. docs/prompts/macros.md notes the easiest way to add it is via Preset Editor > Add Section > Agent. No reference file mentions it.
fix: Document in references/agents.md and character-cards.md. This is the concrete mechanism behind the pass-C 'Add as Prompt Section' finding, and together they qualify the skill's claim that prompt assembly is closed to users — agent output has a supported, first-class injection route.

title: {{outlet::name}} lorebook positioning macro missing
reality: {{outlet::name}} inserts content from lorebook entries whose Position is 'Outlet' and whose Outlet name matches exactly — names are CASE-SENSITIVE, so {{outlet::character_rules}} does not match a differently-cased outlet. Confirmed in macro-engine.ts line 392 and docs/prompts/macros.md line 123.
fix: Add to references/lorebooks.md's entry-position material and to the macro list in character-cards.md. This is a precise placement mechanism for lorebook content — the answer to 'how do I control exactly where this entry lands in the prompt' — and the case-sensitivity gotcha is worth calling out.

title: {{roll:XdY}} and {{lastGenerationType}} missing
reality: {{roll:XdY}} returns a dice-roll total (e.g. {{roll:2d6}}) and resolves even when typed directly into the chat message box. {{lastGenerationType}} yields a plain label from a known set: normal, continue, regenerate, impersonate, guided, autonomous, turn_game, preview, game_setup, lorebook_scan, and others.
fix: Add both to the macro material in references/character-cards.md. {{lastGenerationType}} is especially useful with the conditional macro operators the skill already documents — it enables prompt branches that differ between a normal reply, a regenerate, and an impersonation.

title: Macro coverage is a small fraction of the 58 implemented
reality: macro-engine.ts defines 58 distinct macros. The references cover roughly a dozen. Beyond the families above, uncovered ones include {{charSysInfo}}, {{charPostHistory}}, {{idle_duration}}, {{timezone}}, {{trim}}/{{trimStart}}, {{uppercase}}/{{lowercase}}, and {{noop}}.
fix: Rather than inlining all 58, add a categorised summary table to references/character-cards.md (Context, Variables, Random, Text-transform, Profile, Relocation) plus a pointer to docs/prompts/macros.md as the authoritative full list. The current partial list reads as complete, which is the actual problem.
